newsitem.title: USA: Interneuron says FDA acknowledges error.
newsitem.headline: Interneuron says FDA acknowledges error.

text.p: Interneuron Pharmaceuticals Inc said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration acknowledged it provided incorrect information that a patient had died after using Redux, a prescription treatment for obesity.
Redux was developed by Interneuron and is currently marketed by Wyeth-Ayerst Laboratories, a subsidiary of American Home Products.
Shares of Interneuron gained 2-5/8 to 15-1/2. Wyeth-Ayerst is a unit of American Home Products. American Home Products gained 1-5/8 to 63.
Based on incorrect information provided by the FDA, a news service reported that a patient died "inexplicably" after using Redux for two months.

Interneuron said no such incident had taken place. The FDA said it made an unintentional error in providing the information. The agency said the real case involved a 38-year-old woman who weighed 220 pounds and whose death was judged to be a homicide by a coroner's inquest jury.
The woman's use of Redux is believed to be incidental to the case and did not contribute to her death, the FDA said.

"We have reviewed the incidence of adverse events reported in connection with the use of Redux and do not note any patterns or specific events that are inconsistent with expectations. The data to date regarding Redux do not raise any red flags," FDA spokesman Don McLearn said in a prepared statement.
The news story also refered to the incidence of adverse events related to the use of Redux without providing sufficient context, Interneuron said.
"The story gave credence to unfounded claims by a long-time critic of Redux that the drug may cause brain damage in humans. No evidence of such damage in humans has been reported," Interneuron said.

But Interneuron and American Home Products, in consultation with the FDA and outside experts, said they are continuing to supplement numerous previous safety studies on this issue with additional studies in both animals and humans.
